newsitem.title: CHINA: China top army officer calls for party loyalty.
newsitem.headline: China top army officer calls for party loyalty.

text.p: China's top army officer General Liu Huaqing on Monday called for everlasting loyalty to the Communist Party, saying hostile Western forces were eager to split China.

Hegemonism and power politics still posed a threat to world peace and to China, despite the end of the Cold War, the official Xinhua news agency quoted Liu as telling a meeting of senior army officers in Beijing.
"Some hostile Western forces don't wish to see a unified and powerful socialist China, and have never abandoned their plots of 'Westernising' and 'splitting' China," Xinhua quoted Liu as saying.

"Our military faces a formidable task in protecting national security, guarding the unity of the motherland... and upholding social stability," he said in a speech heralding the 70th anniversary of the August 1 founding of the People's Liberation Army.
Liu, who is one of the seven members of the standing committee of the ruling Communist Party's all-powerful Politburo, called on the armed forces to be unswervingly loyal to the party.

"We must not waver in... placing the barrel of the gun firmly in the hands of those loyal to the party and must guarantee that we obey the party and follow the party at all times and under any circumstances," he said.
Liu, 81, also urged the army to take guidance from President Jiang Zemin, who analysts have said is trying to assert his authority over the three-million strong PLA.
"All soldiers and officers in the army should band tightly together around the party centre with Comrade Jiang Zemin as the core," he said.
Jiang earlier this month issued an internal edict ordering the PLA to crack down on a wave of corruption and crime in its ranks, a move analysts said could be a first step in eventually removing Liu.
